outcome: Dose adjustments for low- and high-risk PPH
Uterotonic usage in presence of comorbidities (pre-eclampsia, cardiac disease)
cohort: The participants were 204 anesthesiologists and obstetricians and gynecologists (OBGYNs) from university-affiliated, government, and private hospitals across Turkey.
finding: There was considerable variability in uterotonic administration practices between anesthesiologists and OBGYNs during cesarean sections.
mod_finding: Anesthesiologists more often favored an intravenous (IV) bolus followed by infusion for low-risk PPH during CS, while OBGYNs preferred IV infusion alone; differences also existed in oxytocin dose increases and combined uterotonic use for high-risk PPH and intrapartum CS.
